CAVEAT 1 (SOURCE ARITHMETIC): Table 2 prints the six SC rows on a flipped scale while all 49 other rows of the same table are raw -- its Mean column equals 5-mean(live) and its Median column equals 6-median(live) (so SC6 is printed as mean 1.019 with SD 0.867, below the 1-5 floor), while SD/EK/Skewness are the untransformed live values. Both flips are uniform across all six items, so the route-1 comparison is unaffected: all 6 items reproduce all five published statistics to <=0.0005. CAVEAT 2 (KEYING, shipped as public_note): in the live table SC6 correlates -0.34..-0.53 with SC1-SC5 while the ten SC1-SC5 pairs correlate +0.56..+0.70, yet Table 3 reports all six loading positively (0.814-0.913, alpha 0.895). Against the rest of the same deposit SC1-SC5 are the reversed ones: they correlate -0.43..-0.53 with the same respondents' procedural-justice items (PJ, positively worded like SC1-SC5) and +0.45..+0.51 with the negated servant-leadership items (EP), while SC6 goes +0.52 with PJ and -0.37 with EP. So for SC1-SC5 a higher stored resp means LESS agreement with the sentence shipped as item_text. This is a direction fact about the response table, not a mapping defect, and it does not disturb which sentence belongs to which code. An alternative reading is that the SC1-SC5 items were administered negated (as the SLS block in this study demonstrably was) and Table 3 printed the un-negated originals; the paper says nothing either way, so the wording is transcribed exactly as printed. RIGHTS: no restriction located and none quotable, so under 'silence is permission' the table ships.
